mechanism: FDA advisory-committee procedure creates a scheduled public-document event before certain open committee meetings. FDA meeting notices state that background/briefing material is intended to be publicly available no later than two business days before the meeting. Those agency and sponsor briefing documents can expose the regulator's evidentiary framing, safety/efficacy concerns and questions before the public committee discussion. The candidate is the document-release clock and newly public regulatory assessment, not the committee vote and not a claim of positive or negative returns.
claim: A future frozen test may ask whether first public release of FDA advisory-committee briefing materials is a causally distinct information event for publicly traded sponsors when the document contains regulator-authored substantive concerns or decision questions that were not already available in prior public filings. No return direction or exploitable alpha is claimed.
prediction: Before any candidate price or return data are opened, admissible events must be selected from FDA advisory-committee notices and meeting-material pages using only the scheduled meeting, document identity, first-public-availability timestamp where reproducible, sponsor/application identity, and pre-specified regulator-document features. Committee votes, meeting-day presentations, subsequent FDA actions and post-event price information are excluded from event selection.
falsification_scope: Kill or park the mechanism if first-public document timestamps cannot be reconstructed point-in-time, if FDA versus sponsor materials cannot be separated deterministically, if substantive concern classification requires outcome-aware judgment, if public prior disclosures make the briefing documents non-incremental in a reproducible sample, or if independent review finds the family duplicates an existing frozen event family.

decision_map.source_clock: FDA advisory-committee meeting announcement and Event Materials publication; intended public release is no later than two business days before the meeting, subject to FDA's stated exception when prior posting is not possible.
decision_map.event_definition: First public availability of FDA-authored or clearly identified combined FDA/sponsor briefing material for an open advisory-committee meeting concerning a named NDA/BLA/sNDA or other sponsor-specific application; freeze document identity and release clock without outcome data.
admissibility: FDA primary meeting notice identifies the application/sponsor and scheduled committee date
briefing material is publicly accessible from FDA
agency-authored versus sponsor-authored material is distinguishable or combined-document provenance is explicit
no price/return data, committee vote, later approval action or future outcome used for selection
decision_map.payer: Any eventual economic effect would have to arise from market participants updating approval-probability, label, safety or evidence-quality beliefs when FDA's previously nonpublic assessment becomes public; this is unproven.
decision_map.capacity_intuition: Potentially limited by low event frequency, rapid professional dissemination, pre-existing sponsor disclosure, heterogeneous applications and uncertainty around exact publication timestamps.
active_disconfirmation: FDA guidance describes a disclosure process but does not establish that briefing documents contain incremental information or that prices underreact.
Meeting announcements themselves can reveal the existence and subject of regulatory scrutiny before briefing materials appear.
Sponsors often disclose trial data and regulatory issues earlier, so apparent briefing-document novelty may be small or absent.
The two-business-day language is an intended deadline with an explicit fallback when FDA cannot post beforehand, so assuming a uniform release clock would be false.
Document tone or 'concern' classification is vulnerable to researcher discretion and must be frozen using outcome-blind rules.
Advisory committees are nonbinding and subsequent FDA decisions must not be used to label the event ex ante.

primary_documentary_evidence.source: FDA Guidance: Preparation and Public Availability of Information Given to Advisory Committee Members (Aug. 2008)
primary_documentary_evidence.fact: FDA describes preparation and public release of sponsor and agency briefing materials for open advisory committee meetings.

next_validator_decision.PASS_TO_TEST_DESIGN: Primary FDA rules, document provenance and point-in-time first-public clock are independently reproducible with outcome-blind feature rules.
next_validator_decision.PARK_DATA: Mechanism is documentary-real but historical publication timestamps or incremental-document classification are not reproducible without leakage.
next_validator_decision.KILL_MECHANISM: Independent review finds no distinct information channel, no reproducible PIT event clock, or duplication with an existing family.
